question.text: The final settlement price for cross-currency futures (e.g., EUR-USD) is computed using:

answer.text: FBIL USD-INR reference rate plus the corresponding FBIL EUR-INR/GBP-INR/JPY-INR exchange rate as applicable
The last traded futures price on expiry day
The RBI reference rate for EUR-USD directly
An average of the last 5 days' closing prices

explanation.text: The Logic: Final settlement for cross-currency futures is computed using the FBIL USD-INR reference rate together with the corresponding FBIL EUR-INR, GBP-INR or JPY-INR rate, depending on which cross-currency pair is being settled. The Trap: The final settlement price is not the last traded futures price and is not a single direct FBIL cross-currency rate. Note: Because the methodology combines two FBIL rates, the settlement value depends on both the relevant cross-currency rate and the USD-INR rate published by FBIL.
